edit.description: `hook()` composes handler members: the authored value carries the group's own fields plus its ordered handlers, so one call mints one group however many handlers it fires. `tapHookRegistration` (:565) composes a single-`command` handler instead of a flat field triple — its `type`/`command` move inside the handler, its `matcher` stays the group's. `Handler` (:386) and `Hook` (:472) are the split the predecessor landed and neither interface moves again, but two doc comments do: :460-:465 says the duplicated fields go when `hook()`'s authoring moves onto `Handler`, and :1926-:1927 says `Hook` carries `Handler`'s `type` union until the same move. This entry IS that move — both sentences become false unless rewritten.

`tapHookRows` (:989) and `registrationRows` (:937) stop being two independent row sources at one collection address: a tap hook whose (event, matcher) an authored group already claims JOINS that group as a further handler rather than minting a second registration row — decision 0075's own consequence, and the fix for this repo's two `PostToolUse` taps (`Skill` and `.*`). `buildTapHookDedupeKey` (:971, used at :995) already keys on the pair, so the join is over the merged set rather than a second pass; the union at :1119 is one of the join's two callers.

The join's second caller, and why it needs one home: `registrationFacts` (:774) independently spreads `[...registrationRows(harness), ...tapHookRows(harness)]` (:775) — the same union `compileDeclarations` writes into `declarations.registrations` (`declarations.ts`:1119), as its own doc says. A join landing in one of the two sites makes the public `RegistrationFact` view and the seam payload disagree on whether a tap joined an authored group. One merged-rows home, both callers reading it (`engineering.md`, "One job, one home").

The gate lift mints temper's own gate as `hook` members (`GATE_HOOKS`, :226, three groups): `gate_hook_fields` (:2383) now returns a group's fields plus its one handler, the `harness.ts` composition loop (:2339-:2346) writes the handler shape, and `module_stems` (:2212) reserves stems against the group grain. `gate_hooks_wired` (:905) and `event_has_command` (:2004) already walk each event's matcher groups, so re-verify rather than rewrite them; `hook_claimed_events` (:1059) claims by event and is unaffected until the address entry. Second site in the same file, named in its own doc as this entry's to retire: `lifted_registration` (:2132) drops a single-handler group's `hooks:` array and hoists that handler's keys onto the lifted member (doc :2116-:2131), a hoist that exists only because today's authoring surface types one handler's keys flat — once `Hook` carries `hooks`, the lift writes the array as read at every handler count, lossless and one branch rather than two.

Re-verify only, and fix what moved: the tap reads a live Claude Code payload (`builtin_kind::classify_claude_code_hook_payload`, called at :252) rather than a member, so nothing here depends on the grain — declared so the entry may correct a doc comment or fixture that spells the old per-handler member shape.

The lift's arms assert the projected `.claude/settings.json` and the composed `harness.ts`; both re-baseline to one group carrying one handler per `GATE_HOOKS` entry. Two fail today under the entry's own work, both here: the gate-hook module shape (the `PreToolUse.ts` `command:`/`matcher:` asserts, :1272-:1280) and the lifted-registration module shape (`SessionStart-2.ts`, :1404-:1412).
The authoring half's twin of the read arms: a `hook()` authoring two handlers emits one registration row and projects one group carrying both.

`a_synthesized_tap_hook_projects_its_matcher_group_through_the_registration_loop` (:750) hand-builds the seam row with a flat `type`/`command`/`matcher` triple and its comment claims that row is "the shape the SDK derives from a telemetry verifier (`sdk/src/declarations.ts`'s `tapHookRows`)". Once `tapHookRegistration` composes a handler, the claim is false and the fixture documents a shape nothing synthesizes: move the fixture with its writer.
The `hook()` authoring cases and the tap-registration case move to the handler-composing shape.

The registration-row cases: one row per group, and a tap hook joining an authored group at the same (event, matcher) rather than appearing twice. Four flat `hook({ name, type, command })` call sites re-spell here (:1934, :1974, :2268, :2269).

The one path outside the prior fence, and the reason no in-fence work reached green: :380 authors `hook({ name: "PreToolUse", type: "command", command: "temper guard" })` as incidental scaffolding inside "emit refuses an edge field naming a target that owns no projection", and `sdk/tsconfig.json` compiles `test/**/*.ts` under `strict` — so that one line reds both the `sdk test` gate and `common::ensure_sdk_built`, taking every SDK-driven Rust test with it. The fix is the one line its siblings take: `hooks: [{ type: "command", command: "temper guard" }]`.

summary: The SDK authors a hook as a group of handlers, and tap synthesis joins an authored group at the same (event, matcher) instead of minting a second.

tests.asserts: a `hook()` carrying two handlers emits one registration row, and a tap hook whose (event, matcher) an authored group already claims joins it as a further handler rather than emitting a second row
the gate lift projects each of temper's three gate hooks as one matcher group carrying one handler, and re-running install is still idempotent

acceptance: `pnpm --dir sdk test` green (strict tsc included), cargo test green, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean. Snapshots need no declaration — `tests/**/snapshots/**` is a standing build surface in chain.ts; the measured run moves none of them.
notes: Decision 0075's second consequence bullet, the authoring side. Split from the engine grain because the two are independently coherent. 0073 (a gate hook is the author's member) is unrouted and lands on these same install.rs surfaces — route it onto this entry, not beside it. Three corpus programs keep the flat spelling and stay green (node type-strips them); they retire in EVERY-AUTHORED-HOOK-SPELLS-ITS-HANDLERS, not here. scoped at 839589ee
